work_order.root_cause: An asymmetry in BUG_10_ROWS at test/web/pages.test.js:3587, between the two halves of one function. The table's eighteen rows are held to BOTH implementations by disagreementsIn, and a row's expected value is what each side must return. Fourteen rows expect [], the !important-divergence row expects the guard [] and the probe ['#main h1 font-size'], and the two real-override rows expect ['#main h1 font-size'] and ['#main h1 line-height'] — all three of those non-empty expectations are ground (a), the h1. The five ground-(b) rows, every one of them a rule that may match the document root, are ':root { all: revert; }', ':root { font: revert; }', ':root { font-size: revert; }', '* { all: revert; }' and '@layer base { :root { all: revert; } }' — all REMOVALS, all expected [] on both sides, and a removal is silent on the root by the contract's own rule (AC-22). A probe that never looked at the root at all therefore returns the same verdict on all five of them as an honest one. The only other assertions that read rootReports are the two shipped-sheet asserts at :3471, `assert.deepEqual(probe.rootReports, [], ...)`, which a permanently-empty array satisfies by construction, and the BUG-11 test's `mustReport` filter, which counts rows whose held value is non-empty — and that count is 3, all ground (a). So the entire ground-(b) claim rests on two empty assertions. The BUG-11 fix correctly made the COMPARISON able to fail, and then left the h1 half as the only thing the table could fail about: `const rootReports = [...new Set(sheet.flatMap(...))]` at :3377 can be made to iterate an empty array, or its reach test moved from the root to the h1, and nothing in 491 cases notices. The h1 half has two rows a silent probe cannot satisfy and a pinned count that says so; the root half has neither. That is the whole defect, and it is in the test contract rather than in shipped code — src/ is correct as it stands and this change touches no production file.
